title: STONE CIRCLE?
description: This site consists of several stones visible about the surface of the thin bog. The area of the project circle (based on the visible stones) is mounded with bog and grass covered, a distinct green amid the darker surrounding bog. Towards the centre of the circle is a large stone slab that was erected several years ago by the landlord. The site is located c.1km SE of Clogherny Wedge Tomb [TYR 011:018] in shallow bogland with excellent views S down the valley. The visible stones stand 0.2-0.4m above the surface of the bog, which is c.0.2m deep. It is difficult to say definitely if this is part of a stone circle or perhaps a kerb around the mound.

title: STONE CIRCLE?
description: In an upland area with land falling to WSW, with excellent views S-SW. This site is described in PSAMNI as "an irregular mound of standing stones". The site is very disturbed & consists of 3-4 stones in situ. The tallest upright is at ESE, 0.83m high x 0.48m x 0.3m, tapering to a point. 5.81m to WSW is a 2nd stone, 1.2m long, x 0.45 x 0.38. 4m WNW of the 1st stone is another stone in situ, not as tall as the 1st two. A 4th is set near the fence at SSE. It is very small & squat & is not certainly part of the stone circle/megalithic tomb. The site is too disturbed to categorise & could be a either a stone circle or a disturbed tomb. There are a few other large stones lying around, but not in situ.

title: STONE CIRCLE
description: This "remarkable stonehenge" recorded in this townland  seems to have been destroyed. A local farmer pointed out the area where the stone circle stood. He said there were once up to 12 stones, some 2m long, which lay in a heap next to the now disused house on the site. Several of these have been used elsewhere on the McNeill farm. According to the OS memoirs, destruction of the stone circle had been ongoing for c.50 years at that time, with some stones "...blasted with gun-powder because they hindered ploughing". Mr.McNeill has found, in the area of the site & elsewhere, many stone & flint artefacts, including 3 porcellanite axes, a leaf-shaped arrowhead, 2 lozenge arrowheads & a barbed & tanged arrowhead.

title: STONE CIRCLE
description: This site is described in UJA 1939 as "...Plain circle 37ft in diam." although the published co-ordinates are wrong. The circle is set just below 900ft on a S-facing hill slope, with extensive views all round, except N. Nearby turf banks indecated that the area is cut-away bog, which has been improved to create sheep pasture. Eight stones of the circle can be seen protruding from the ground, to a max. height of 0.5m. Seven of these stones are set along the N & NE edge of the circle, with only 2 standing to mark the southern extent. The circle measures 10.6m E-W x 11.3m N-S, although the fallen stones on the W side make exact measurements difficult. This W edge has been partially disturbed by an old laneway  or ditch which runs past.

title: Stone Circle
description:
Stone circle situated on limestone terrace. (1) NGR corrected by Y Luke. (2)

Stone Circle
Stone circle made up of more than a dozen low limestone boulders in sub-circular formation c.12.4 x 11.4. Many of the boulders barely break through the turf that covers them. It appears to be intact and its low profile is probably not due to robbing. There is a small low cairn outlier just to the south-west. It lies on a limestone terrace just beneath the main limestone plateau which surrounds Ingleborough by Harry Hallam's Moss.
Surveyed by Yvonne Luke and the Ingleborough Archaeological Group 2007-8

title: Stone circle
description:
Small stone circle, possibly Bronze Age, 33ft in diameter. One third of the circle robbed but other stones standing - reported by A Raistrick (1)

SE0307 6402. A small stone circle comprised of five surviving stones forming a half-circle with a diameter of about 10 metres; possibly of Bronze Age date.  This monument is sited on Mossy Moor north east of SM24475 (MYD4403) , a scheduled stone circle believed to be of Bronze Age date.  Located by Chris Knowles, English Heritage Field Monument Warden (letter of 28 April 1997). "It is slightly less obvious than the scheduled circle but I am reasonably confident of the identification. There is not much random stone visible on the surface of the moor and some of the stones in the circle are not in a natural position, having been placed on edge. The two circles are similar in this and other respects."  NB  A Raistrick's notes refer to a second stone circle on Mossy Moor; this is probably it. (2)

A near-complete ring of eight stones, arranged in a circle with a gap on the east side.  None of the stones are higher or longer than 3 feet.  At least three of them seemed to have been set along their longer axis rather than being set in the tall upright position. Peeling back of heather vegetation suggested two  stones had what seems like small packing stones at one end where it seemed obvious they had stood upright. In the centre of the circule is a small but distinct scattering of stones, very much like a denuded cairn. (3)

title: STONE CIRCLE
description: On gently sloping ground in reclaimed pasture. High rocky ground including scarp stretches away to N & the lowlands of E. Tyrone stretch away to SE. This site was reported by the owner, who observed it during turf cutting. The stones are somewhat uncharacteristic of stone circles in the area, being boulder shaped. However, 16 firmly bedded stones, ranging 0.25-0.55m high & 2 very equal diameters, 11.5m along opposing axes, independently establish the validity of this site.

title: STONE CIRCLE
description: On a slight knoll in rather boggy ground. The monument consists of 16 visible largish stones set in an oval which is 16.4m E-W & 13m N-S. One at S is set radially, which may indicate an entrance or false entrance (see UJA 2, 1939, 4, fig. 2 where more stones are visible). The average height of the stones is 0.8m & in general they have flat faces which are turned towards the centre; the tallest, which is 1.5m high, faces WSW of centre. there is no sign of the structure mentioned in PSAMNI, 214.  A field fence cuts through the site NNE-SSW & an animal track runs N-S through the site.

title: possible STONE CIRCLE & STANDING STONE
description: This site is not shown as an antiquity by the OS and was reported to EHS by a local informant. It lies on gently sloping ground, falling to SE & rising to NW, with good views E-SW, but overlooked to W. A number of stones are visible, forming a gently arc immediately S of a field boundary. They are 0.2-0.6m high, up to 1.2m wide and on average 0.35m thick. Several to NE look like they may have been dumped here, but others have been incorporated into the field boundary and have obviously been here for some time. A previously unrecorded standing stone, 1.25m high & 0.6m wide & thick is visible on slightly higher ground 12m N of the field boundary. This appears to be the remains of a damaged stone circle.

title: Stone Circle
description:
Stone circle. (1)

A large and well defined stone circle averaging 25.0m in diameter, formed by six free-standing boulders of millstone grit. Within the enclosed area is a small embanked circle and a stony mound. The latter feature could represent debris from a partial clearance of the stones (no stone holes are apparent, however, in the perimeter of the circle) though the purpose of the circular bank is obscure. A survey and enlarged plan have been made. (2)

The circle now falls in afforestation, and is no longer recognizable. Most of the stones, none of which (from previous report) was large, appear to have been dislodged or buried in the course of planting. The small embanked circle (see enlarged sketch) survives, although ploughed through. Its diameter is approximately 6.0m, and the breaks in the bank confirm a stony construction. Beyond this, little can be said as to its possible function. Survey of 10/2/64 cancelled. (3)

title: STONE CIRCLE
description: The area consists of a SW-facing slope of a terraced hill side, the upper slopes of which are marsh & bogland. The lower slopes have been heavily drained & extensively reclaimed. Numerous large rounded boulders are strewn across the area, but none of them appear likely candidates for disturbed standing stones. Despite extensive search of a wide area the site was not located, nor was there any local knowledge of it.
